originalTitle: Cocoa prices are easing. So why is chocolate still so expensive?
summary: Chocolate firms look to win shoppers back with premium products and social media trends after poor weather conditions, tariffs, and the Iran war hit sales.
content:
Cocoa prices are beginning to ease after a record-breaking rally, but don't expect cheaper candy just yet as the world's biggest chocolate makers turn to social media-inspired products and other strategies to win shoppers back.

Cocoa prices reached record highs over the past two years, triggered by adverse weather conditions and poor cocoa harvests that pushed chocolate costs higher and dampened consumer sentiment.

However, the price of cocoa now appears to be falling.

Cocoa futures were last trading at $5327 per metric ton and are down 34% over the past year. The commodity surged to almost $12,000 per metric ton at the end of 2024. Cocoa prices typically hovered around $2,000 to $3,000 over the past two decades.

Swiss Chocolate giants Barry Callebaut , Lindt , and Nestlé all pointed to soaring cocoa prices as a drag on earnings.

Lindt said Monday that groupwide price increases of 11.8% led to chocolate sales volumes dropping 7.5% as fewer shoppers bought chocolate in the first half of the year.

"Record cocoa prices required unprecedented price increases across the industry, while geopolitical uncertainty, inflation and weak consumer sentiment weighed on demand," Group CEO Adalbert Lechner said in an analyst call. "The crisis in the Middle East added another headwind with weaker tourism flows from Asia and the Middle East to Europe."

The world's largest chocolate and cocoa supplier, Barry Callebaut, said that while global consumers are buying 4.4% less chocolate in the third quarter than the same time last year, overall sales volumes for the company grew 5.7% in the quarter, turning positive for the first time in over two years. Additionally, its global cocoa sales accelerated 18% due to a market correction earlier this year.

Meanwhile, food and beverage firm Nestlé said higher cocoa and coffee prices hit its underlying trading operating profit in the first half of the year, dropping 2.8%. The firm's confectionery business makes up 9.7% of its total sales. Nestlé expects to see margins benefit from cocoa prices coming down.

Cocoa prices' volatile run was largely due to poor cocoa harvests in West Africa, which were worsened by weather patterns related to El Niño and climate change, resulting in tight supply.

El Niño is a weather phenomenon with warmer-than-average temperatures that occurs every two to seven years in the Pacific Ocean. Soaring cocoa prices in 2024 were largely due to a 'strong' El Niño that led to drier, hotter weather and erratic rainfall in West Africa, according to a December analysis by Dr Tanya Lander, a researcher at the Oxford Martin School Programme on the Future of Food.

"So, it is unsurprising that the El Niño weather was linked to poor cocoa harvests in both Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana (where 60-70% of global cocoa beans are produced)," Lander wrote.

Climate change and increasing temperatures are also playing a role, with 2024 being the hottest year on record. A recent heatwave across Europe could also dampen consumer enthusiasm for chocolate, UBS analysts said in an early July note on Lindt.

Heatwaves and rising temperatures in some of Lindt's core European markets could impact chocolate demand, with European sales excluding Eastern Europe, declining in the four weeks ending June 14, the analysts said.

However, Barry Callebaut said that while a strong El Niño has been confirmed for 2026 and 2027 and creates a downside risk on supply, a large surplus for 2025-2026 acts as a buffer, resulting in a very different situation from 2023-2024.

The UBS analysts expect that Lindt has hedged at favourable cocoa bean prices for 2027, a move they estimate could reduce costs by as much as 500 million Swiss francs.

Meanwhile, U.S. President Donald Trump's reciprocal tariffs have also had a brief but significant impact, causing price spikes and supply chain disruptions. More recently, the conflict in the Middle East also hit Lindt's travel retail business globally by reducing tourism flows.

Premium chocolate, social media trends

As cocoa prices are expected to recover, chocolatiers are looking to win back their core customer base by innovating their premium product formats, as well as keeping a closer eye on social media trends that young people are engaging with.

Lindt released its Dubai-style chocolate bar in December 2024, a in a bid to capitalize on a viral social media trend . Global retailers from Walmart to Trader Joe's, Shake Shack , and Harrods are now selling Dubai chocolate too.

Lindt CEO Lechner said the company plans to expand its "social media presence" to create a seamless journey between inspiration, discovery, and purchase.

"The extraordinary success of our Dubai Style Chocolate launch demonstrated the growing power of social media in building awareness, engagement, and demand for our brands," Lechner said in the earnings call.

"This strategy is helping us reach new audiences and strengthen our relevance with younger consumers."

Nestlé's CEO Philipp Navratil echoed this view, saying in an analyst call on Thursday that the company plans to invest more in influencer marketing, with changes coming to how the brand advertises itself.

"More digital, more social, more organic, more fun. Tapping into how younger consumers engage with the world," Navratil said.

Both Barry Callebaut and Lindt are focusing on consumer interest in premium products for the remaining half of the year, but they're getting creative about how they offer products rather than increasing prices.

"By broadening our price architecture, we can attract new consumers, increase purchase frequency, and offer more touchpoints with the Lindt brand without compromising our premium positioning," Lechner said.

Lechner pointed out that Lindt had selectively lower prices in key markets such as Germany and Switzerland, particularly over Christmas, to support consumer demand during its most important season. Meanwhile, Barry Callebaut and Nestlé haven't mentioned lowering prices.

chineseTitle: 可可价格正在回落。那么为什么巧克力仍然这么贵呢？
chineseSummary: 在恶劣的天气条件、关税和伊朗战争影响销售之后，巧克力公司希望通过优质产品和社交媒体趋势重新赢得购物者的青睐。
chineseContent:
可可价格在创纪录的上涨后开始回落，但随着全球最大的巧克力制造商转向社交媒体启发的产品和其他策略来赢回购物者，不要指望糖果会变得更便宜。

过去两年，可可价格创下历史新高，原因是恶劣的天气条件和可可收成不佳，推高了巧克力成本并抑制了消费者信心。

然而，可可的价格现在似乎正在下跌。

可可期货最新交易价格为每吨 5327 美元，较去年下跌 34%。到 2024 年底，该商品价格飙升至每吨近 12,000 美元。过去二十年里，可可价格通常徘徊在 2,000 至 3,000 美元左右。

瑞士巧克力巨头百乐嘉利宝 (Barry Callebaut)、瑞士莲 (Lindt) 和雀巢 (Nestlé) 均指出可可价格飙升拖累了盈利。

Lindt 周一表示，由于今年上半年购买巧克力的消费者减少，集团范围内价格上涨 11.8%，导致巧克力销量下降 7.5%。

集团首席执行官阿达尔伯特·莱赫纳（Adalbert Lechner）在分析师电话会议上表示：“创纪录的可可价格需要整个行业前所未有的价格上涨，而地缘政治的不确定性、通货膨胀和疲软的消费者信心对需求造成了压力。” “中东危机又增加了一个阻力，从亚洲和中东到欧洲的旅游流量疲软。”

全球最大的巧克力和可可供应商百乐嘉利宝表示，虽然第三季度全球消费者购买的巧克力比去年同期减少了 4.4%，但该公司第三季度的整体销量增长了 5.7%，两年多来首次转正。此外，由于今年早些时候的市场调整，其全球可可销量增长了 18%。

与此同时，食品和饮料公司雀巢表示，可可和咖啡价格上涨影响了其上半年的基本营业利润，下降了 2.8%。该公司的糖果业务占其总销售额的9.7%。雀巢预计利润率将因可可价格下跌而受益。

可可价格波动主要是由于西非可可收成不佳，而厄尔尼诺现象和气候变化相关的天气模式使可可收成恶化，导致供应紧张。

厄尔尼诺现象是一种气温高于平均水平的天气现象，每两到七年在太平洋发生一次。牛津马丁学院未来食品项目研究员 Tanya Lander 博士 12 月的分析显示，2024 年可可价格飙升主要是由于“强烈”厄尔尼诺现象导致西非天气更加干燥、炎热和降雨不稳定。

兰德写道：“因此，厄尔尼诺天气与科特迪瓦和加纳（全球 60-70% 的可可豆产地）的可可歉收有关，这并不奇怪。”

气候变化和气温升高也起到了一定作用，2024 年是有记录以来最热的一年。瑞银分析师在 7 月初关于 Lindt 的报告中表示，最近欧洲各地的热浪也可能削弱消费者对巧克力的热情。

分析师表示，瑞士莲一些核心欧洲市场的热浪和气温上升可能会影响巧克力需求，截至 6 月 14 日的四个星期内，欧洲销量（不包括东欧）出现下降。

不过，百乐嘉利宝表示，虽然2026年和2027年已确认出现强烈的厄尔尼诺现象，并对供应造成下行风险，但2025-2026年的大量盈余起到了缓冲作用，导致2023-2024年的情况截然不同。

瑞银分析师预计，Lindt 已在 2027 年以有利的可可豆价格进行对冲，他们估计此举可减少多达 5 亿瑞士法郎的成本。

与此同时，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普的互惠关税也产生了短暂但重大的影响，导致价格飙升和供应链中断。最近，中东冲突还导致游客流量减少，从而打击了瑞士莲的全球旅游零售业务。

优质巧克力，社交媒体趋势

随着可可价格预计回升，巧克力制造商希望通过创新优质产品形式以及密切关注年轻人参与的社交媒体趋势来赢回核心客户群。

Lindt 于 2024 年 12 月推出了迪拜风格的巧克力棒，旨在利用社交媒体的病毒式传播趋势。从沃尔玛到 Trader Joe's、Shake Shack 和 Harrods 等全球零售商现在也在销售迪拜巧克力。

Lindt首席执行官莱赫纳表示，该公司计划扩大其“社交媒体影响力”，以打造灵感、发现和购买之间的无缝旅程。

莱赫纳在财报电话会议上表示：“我们推出的迪拜风格巧克力取得了巨大成功，这证明了社交媒体在提高我们品牌的知名度、参与度和需求方面的力量日益增强。”

“这一战略正在帮助我们吸引新的受众并加强我们与年轻消费者的相关性。”

雀巢首席执行官菲利普·纳夫拉蒂尔（Philipp Navratil）也赞同这一观点，他在周四的分析师电话会议上表示，该公司计划在影响力营销上投入更多资金，并改变该品牌的自我广告方式。

“更加数字化、更加社交化、更加有机、更加有趣。探索年轻消费者与世界互动的方式，”纳夫拉蒂尔说。

百乐嘉利宝和瑞士莲在今年下半年都将重点放在消费者对优质产品的兴趣上，但他们在提供产品的方式上发挥了创意，而不是提高价格。

莱赫纳表示：“通过扩大我们的价格架构，我们可以吸引新消费者，提高购买频率，并在不影响我们高端定位的情况下提供更多与瑞士莲品牌的接触点。”

莱赫纳指出，瑞士莲有选择地降低了德国和瑞士等关键市场的价格，特别是在圣诞节期间，以支持最重要季节的消费者需求。与此同时，百乐嘉利宝和雀巢都没有提到降价。

因斯泰亚
